purpose: Time-gap test (27 Sep 2026): the GPU context network at 16, 24 and 32 epochs (otherwise the ctx_e32 settings of configs/adsb_ctx_network_v3.json) fitted on January-June 2025 ('gap') and on May-October 2025 ('near', same six-month size), both scoring November and December 2025. Question: does the longer-trained network's advantage shrink as the scored months move further from the fitted ones? v30 (more 32-epoch weight) transferred only ~6% of its development gain, against >100% for earlier network rounds; the ranking months lie 1-18 months after the twelve-month refit while every development fold has a 0-1 month gap. Descriptive test; any recipe change it motivates needs its own declared round.

features.contract: the x19 committee learners: 276 timeline bundle features + 27 ADS-B departure/neighbour features + 11 v19 features (314)

readings.per_fold: 4-seed mean prediction per variant; RMSE on non-LIRF November+December rows (all, matched, unmatched) and by month
readings.interaction: (g32 - g16) and (g24 - g16) RMSE differences in 'gap' vs 'near', with a paired-day bootstrap interval of the difference-in-differences
readings.note: g32/g24 in 'near' should reproduce the development ordering (32 > 24 > 16 epochs); a smaller or reversed advantage in 'gap' supports down-weighting long training for the ranking months
